title: Design DHFR FRET fusion gBlock
query: Design a gBlock encoding a DHFR-containing fusion protein to be cloned into a plasmid, for an experiment testing DHFR stability by FRET with an excitation filter passing 505 nm and an emission filter passing 610 nm. The fusion protein must be pull-downable onto beads coated with molecules having SMILES Nc3nc(OCc1ccccc1)c2nc[nH]c2n3 and must bind the antibody whose heavy- and light-chain sequences are in antibody.fasta. Store the gBlock sequence and nothing else (no empty lines) in /app/gblock.txt. The gBlock may encode only GS linkers and the molecule binding protein, antibody binding protein, donor, acceptor, and DHFR. The molecule binding protein, donor, and acceptor must each encode only proteins found in /app/pdb_ids.txt, with protein sequences matching the FASTA returned by the PDB API for the encoded PDB ID. The antibody binder need not match a protein in /app/pdb_ids.txt; it should encode the protein for which the antibody was designed, using only the most common variant and not repeating it even if repetition increases binding affinity. Reuse the DHFR protein sequence found in plasmid.gb. Do not include start or stop codons. Remove the N-terminal methionine from every protein sequence. The donor and acceptor must be separated only by DHFR and GS linkers. The donor and acceptor peak emission/excitation must match the filter cube exactly according to FPbase API data. There must be no GS linkers at the N or C terminus. There must be a GS linker between every subprotein, and linkers between different subproteins must be 5-20 amino acids long. Any 50-nucleotide window encoding the fusion protein must have 30-70% GC content. The gBlock must be at most 3000 nucleotides long. The N-to-C order of subproteins must be antibody binder - donor - DHFR - acceptor - molecule binder.
review_flags: Donor/acceptor identities are not named; they must be inferred from FPbase API spectra matching 505 nm excitation and 610 nm emission.
Molecule-binding protein identity is not named; it must be inferred from the supplied SMILES and /app/pdb_ids.txt.
Antibody binder identity/variant is not named; it must be inferred from antibody.fasta.
The task references /app/pdb_ids.txt, plasmid.gb, antibody.fasta, and external PDB/FPbase APIs whose contents are not supplied in the message.
